issues: Critical safety hazard: max_iob_units is set to 25 U, which exceeds the total daily dose and provides no ceiling for runaway SMB delivery.
High Time Below Range (5.1% overall) driven by extreme nocturnal hypoglycemia, reaching 18.5% at 01:00.
Repeated massive glucose crashes (drops over 100 mg/dL) following UAM-triggered microbolus stacking.
Complete lack of entered carbohydrates prevents Carb Ratio (CR) evaluation and leaves the algorithm without Carbs on Board (COB) constraints.
summary: The system is operating exclusively in an unannounced meal (UAM) mode without logged carbohydrates. While overall time in range is adequate, aggressive automation settings combined with a very high maximum IOB limit are driving severe insulin stacking. This results in dangerous late-night hypoglycemia and massive post-rise crashes, likely exacerbated by delayed digestion from GLP-1 therapy.
education: GLP-1 medications slow gastric emptying, causing meals to absorb much later and flatter than usual.

When UAM (Unannounced Meals) manages un-logged food, it reacts to the rising glucose by issuing microboluses. If the rise is slow and prolonged (as with GLP-1), UAM can easily overshoot if not constrained by a tight max IOB limit.

The max_iob_units setting is the ultimate safety ceiling for closed-loop systems. It should typically be a fraction of your total daily dose to prevent catastrophic hypoglycemia in the event of a false sensor rise or prolonged spike.
strengths: Excellent CGM data coverage (98.7%) with very few gaps.
Algorithm successfully identifies and attacks rising glucose levels automatically.
Consistent sensor wear and routine profile switching noted.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
Immediate action is strongly recommended to reduce max_iob_units. 25 U is profoundly unsafe for a user whose total daily dose is ~20 U.
Overnight glucose targets of 90 mg/dL are too aggressive while experiencing 18.5% Time Below Range at 01:00.

analysis_steps.findings: The severe nocturnal hypoglycemia and massive correction crashes are driven by UAM having no COB constraints, combined with an unsafe 25 U max IOB limit and overly tight 90 mg/dL overnight targets.

recommendations.title: Reduce max_iob_units immediately
recommendations.description: A max IOB limit of 25 U exceeds your total daily dose. This completely removes the algorithm's safety ceiling, allowing UAM to stack massive amounts of insulin and cause severe crashes.

recommendations.title: Raise overnight targets
recommendations.description: Targeting 90 mg/dL overnight while using an unannounced meal strategy and a GLP-1 medication is pushing the system into severe nocturnal hypoglycemia (18.5% TBR at 1 AM).

recommendations.title: Begin logging carbohydrates
recommendations.description: To prevent UAM from overshooting, the algorithm needs to know roughly how many carbs are active (COB). Even if no immediate bolus is given, logging the carbs restricts runaway insulin delivery.

profile_recommendation.rationale: A target of 90 mg/dL starting at 23:00 and 00:00 is too aggressive. Combined with delayed digestion from GLP-1 and active UAM, the system drives glucose into severe hypoglycemia (over 18% TBR at 01:00).
profile_recommendation.next_check: Observe overnight stability for 3-5 days after raising the targets and reducing max_iob_units.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Raise the 00:00 and 23:00 glucose targets from 90 mg/dL to 110 mg/dL.

meal_strategy_summary.rationale: The system acts fully reactively on Unannounced Meals (UAM). GLP-1 slows digestion, causing UAM to over-deliver early in the rise resulting in massive late crashes because there are no logged carbohydrates (COB) to throttle the algorithm's expectations.
meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Log approximate carbohydrate amounts when eating to provide the algorithm with Carbs on Board (COB), even if you choose not to deliver an immediate bolus.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log carbs for 5 days and observe if providing a COB boundary reduces the UAM correction overshoots.

implementation_steps: Reduce max_iob_units to a safe fraction of your total daily dose immediately (e.g., 6 U) to restore the algorithm's safety ceiling.
Raise the 00:00 and 23:00 target glucose levels to 110 mg/dL to provide a larger buffer against overnight hypoglycemia.
Monitor overnight glucose stability for 3 to 5 days.
Begin logging carbohydrate entries for meals so the algorithm can properly calculate COB decay instead of blindly guessing via UAM.
